why: Notice the diagram is generated from getBoundingClientRect on the five stage columns, and that one place(p) drives wire, head, stops, text dimming and three count-ups together, so a steps section shows the real mechanism with 5 lane labels and one job's numbers instead of numbered circles.

Notice each column swaps the usual icon for a real identifier from the buyer's own logs and then holds three beats (cause, fix, limit), with hierarchy built from one pink tag, one display-serif title and 15px body and no card chrome at all.

Notice 8 rows by 5 columns gives 40 specific data points on 20/20/40/10/10 widths, hierarchy comes from a single 500 weight on the first column, one row admits a rollback, and hover inverts the row and indents its first cell 10px.

Notice the signup is one 430px field while the proof is three 1/3/1 rows of date, display-serif title and read time, each opening to a real story with no JS for the state change, so the archive itself is the pitch.

Notice the form has exactly one input whose placeholder models the answer, three prefill buttons that write the visitor's sentence for them, and small print carrying a price range and two refusals, so the contact section does the qualifying.
